jobs.title: Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence-FR
jobs.description:
Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 130,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

Join our team!

Position Summary

The Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence leads the enterprise data function for Top Aces. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director defines how data is governed, integrated, protected, and used across aviation operations, maintenance and engineering, supply chain, finance, safety, quality, human resources, commercial programs, and executive management.

The role will establish trusted enterprise data products and decision-ready analytics while respecting aviation record integrity, contractual obligations, export controls, data residency, and need-to-know access. A central priority is to improve the quality and usability of data from Ramco and connected systems so that leaders and front-line teams can manage aircraft availability, maintenance execution, material readiness, program performance, and financial results with greater confidence.

Top Aces Business Context

Top Aces provides advanced operational training and aircraft sustainment services to Canada, the United States, NATO members, and allied nations. The company operates globally in a safety-critical and security-sensitive environment that combines flight operations, maintenance and repair, engineering, supply chain, training, and proprietary technology. The data environment therefore requires strong governance across business units, legal entities, jurisdictions, and security domains.

The Director will translate these operating realities into an enterprise data strategy that supports growth, operational readiness, regulatory compliance, and disciplined investment. The role must balance standardization with the access boundaries required for Canadian, U.S., and international programs.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy and Operating Model

Partner with the CIO to develop and execute a multi-year enterprise data and BI strategy aligned with Top Aces' business strategy, operating model, technology roadmap, and investment priorities.
Create a practical data operating model that defines decision rights, ownership, stewardship, architecture standards, delivery methods, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.
Chair or support the enterprise data governance council and maintain a prioritized roadmap based on operational value, regulatory risk, data quality, and delivery capacity.
Partner with the CIO and U.S. IT and security leadership to establish appropriate data segregation, access controls, and technology control plans for FOCI-related and export-controlled environments, where applicable.

Data Governance Quality and Protection

Establish enterprise policies and standards for data ownership, classification, quality, lineage, retention, archival, residency, access, and acceptable use.
Define authoritative sources and common business terms for critical domains, including aircraft, fleets, components, serialized parts, maintenance programs, work orders, defects, inventory, suppliers, customers, contracts, personnel, and financial dimensions.
Implement data quality controls, issue-management workflows, and scorecards that identify root causes and assign corrective action to accountable data owners.
Work with Cybersecurity, Legal, Export Compliance, Privacy, Quality, and program security personnel to protect personal, proprietary, controlled, and customer information throughout its lifecycle.
Ensure analytics and data-sharing practices comply with applicable contractual clauses, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR requirements, privacy laws, and customer security obligations.

Data Architecture Integration and Platforms

Define the target enterprise data architecture, including ingestion, integration, master and reference data, lakehouse or warehouse services, semantic models, reporting, metadata, and monitoring.
Establish integration patterns and data contracts for Ramco and other enterprise platforms using secure APIs, event-based interfaces, ETL or ELT pipelines, and controlled file exchange where required.
Reduce duplicate datasets and spreadsheet-dependent reporting by creating reusable, governed data products and certified semantic models.
Set engineering standards for observability, reconciliation, change control, testing, performance, resilience, backup, and recovery across the data platform.
Manage the data-platform lifecycle, capacity, licensing, vendor performance, and total cost of ownership, with particular attention to Microsoft Fabric, Azure data services, Power BI, and connected technologies.

Aviation and MRO Data

Lead data remediation and governance for Ramco MRO and ERP, focusing on master data, transactional integrity, usability, reporting structures, and interfaces with finance, supply chain, engineering, and flight operations.
Partner with Maintenance, Engineering, Airworthiness, Quality, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve the completeness and consistency of aircraft configuration, component history, flight hours and cycles, maintenance plans, work packages, defects, technical records, and inventory data.
Preserve the integrity and auditability of approved maintenance and airworthiness records while enabling controlled downstream analytics.
Develop trusted measures for aircraft availability, dispatch reliability, mission-capable status, maintenance schedule compliance, turnaround time, component reliability, inventory availability, and aircraft-on-ground events.
Support data readiness for operational and regulatory audits, customer reporting, contract performance reviews, and fleet-planning decisions.

Business Intelligence and Performance Management

Lead the design and delivery of executive, operational, and functional dashboards using consistent definitions, clear ownership, and traceable data sources.
Build an enterprise performance framework that connects mission delivery, safety, fleet readiness, maintenance, supply chain, program, customer, workforce, and financial measures.
Develop governed self-service analytics so business users can answer routine questions without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive data.
Improve forecasting and scenario analysis for fleet utilization, maintenance demand, materials, labour capacity, contract delivery, revenue, cash flow, and program profitability.
Maintain a transparent intake and prioritization process for BI requests, balancing regulatory deadlines, operational urgency, enterprise reuse, and expected value.

Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and govern analytics and AI use cases such as predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring.
Require documented business ownership, suitable data quality, human oversight, security review, and measurable benefits before analytics or AI solutions move into production.
Coordinate with engineering, operations, and technology teams when operational, training, mission-system, or live and synthetic data may be used, ensuring the work remains within approved classification and authorization boundaries.
Monitor model performance, data drift, access, and business outcomes, and retire solutions that no longer meet operational, security, or financial requirements.

Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership

Build and lead a capable team spanning data governance, architecture, engineering, BI, and analytics; define roles, develop talent, and manage succession for critical skills.
Partner with executives and functional leaders to convert business questions into governed data products, clear measures, and practical decisions.
Create an active network of business data owners and stewards and hold regular reviews of quality, adoption, access, and value realization.
Manage external partners and vendors through clear outcomes, architecture standards, service levels, security requirements, and commercial accountability.
Communicate data risks, progress, tradeoffs, and investment needs to senior leadership in concise business terms.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, data engineering, analytics, business, engineering, or a related discipline. A graduate degree or relevant professional certification is an asset.
At least 10 years of progressive experience in data management, analytics, BI, enterprise applications, or data architecture, including at least five years leading teams or major cross-functional programs.
Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting in a complex ERP or MRO environment. Direct experience with Ramco is a significant asset; experience with comparable aviation or enterprise platforms is also relevant.
Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, including Canada and the United States, is preferred.

Technical and Regulatory Knowledge

Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modelling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL or ELT integration.
Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI technologies. Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and Microsoft data services is preferred.
Working knowledge of aviation maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.
Familiarity with aviation regulatory and quality environments such as Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, safety management systems, and AS9100 is an asset.
Working knowledge of information classification, access control, auditability, privacy, data residency, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR, CUI safeguards, CMMC, and NIST SP 800-171, as applicable to the role and programs supported.
Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearances, controlled-goods eligibility, and customer or program authorizations required for the position.

Leadership Competencies

Business judgment that connects data investment to safety, mission readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.
Ability to influence executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users without relying solely on formal authority.
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data limitations, security constraints, and architectural decisions to non-technical audiences.
Disciplined program leadership, with practical experience managing priorities, budgets, vendors, risks, and organizational change.
Commitment to Top Aces' values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together.

Requisition ID: 278435

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

Purpose

The Director, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management & Governance
leads the enterprise approach to identifying, assessing, and controlling risks arising from the use of artificial intelligence across the bank. The role defines and operates the AI risk management standard, sets guardrails that allow AI to scale safely, and partners with the business, technology, and the risk and control functions to ensure AI is trusted, explainable, and compliant with Canadian and U.S. regulatory expectations.

Is this role right for you? In this role, you will be involved in:

AI Risk Management Standard

Own the design, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the AI risk management standard, in alignment with Bank policies, including acceptable use and AI ethics requirements.
Align the framework with applicable regulations and industry standards, such as OSFI E-23, U.S. Federal Reserve model risk guidance (SR 11-7), and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework.
Maintain the AI control catalogue and map AI-specific risks to existing risk taxonomy categories, including model, privacy, third-party, cyber, operational, legal, and conduct risk.

AI Intake, Assessment, and Oversight

Lead the AI risk assessment process, including tiering of use cases by risk, Trusted AI assessments, and required mitigations before deployment.
Provide risk-based guidance and approval recommendations for generative AI and other emerging use cases, including conditions for client-facing or external use.
Maintain the enterprise AI inventory and monitor use cases for ongoing compliance, performance, bias, explainability, and drift.
Establish guardrails and restrictions for higher-risk capabilities, such as agentic AI, until governance and controls are in place.

Governance, Reporting, and Regulatory Engagement

Support Data and AI steering groups and governance forums, with clear decision rights and escalation paths.
Produce executive reporting on AI risk exposure, key risk indicators, issues, and remediation progress.
Serve as a primary contact for regulators, internal audit, and second- and third-line functions on AI risk matters.
Track the evolving regulatory and industry landscape and translate changes into practical requirements for the bank.

Partnership and Leadership

Partner with Scotia Intelligence, Harbour, technology, and business lines to embed AI risk controls into delivery and the data lifecycle.
Collaborate with Model Risk, Privacy, Legal, Compliance, Cybersecurity, and Third-Party Risk to ensure consistent, non-duplicative oversight.
Lead and develop a team of AI risk professionals, fostering a culture of accountability, curiosity, and responsible innovation.
Promote AI risk awareness through training, guidance, and clear, business-friendly communication.

Direct Reports
: 4+

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed? We’d love to work with you if you have the following:

10+ years of progressive experience in AI risk, model risk, data risk, technology risk, responsible AI, or a related risk/governance discipline within a complex organization.
7+ years of leadership experience, including experience building, leading, and developing high-performing teams.
Demonstrated experience developing and implementing enterprise AI, model, data, or technology risk management frameworks, standards, controls, and governance processes.
Strong understanding of AI and emerging technology risks, including generative AI, model performance, explainability, bias and fairness, privacy, third-party risk, cybersecurity, and responsible AI considerations.
Knowledge of relevant AI and model risk regulatory requirements and industry frameworks, including OSFI E-23, SR 11-7, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and evolving AI regulatory expectations.
Proven experience translating regulatory, risk, and technical requirements into practical controls, standards, processes, and guidance that enable responsible business adoption.
Strong strategic and analytical capabilities, with demonstrated experience influencing senior leaders and partnering across business, technology, risk, compliance, legal, privacy, cybersecurity, and other control functions.
Excellent relationship management and communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex AI and risk concepts clearly to technical, business, executive, audit, and regulatory audiences.

Join our team!

Position Summary

The Director of Data Management and Business Intelligence leads the enterprise data function for Top Aces. Reporting to the Chief Information Officer, the Director defines how data is governed, integrated, protected, and used across aviation operations, maintenance and engineering, supply chain, finance, safety, quality, human resources, commercial programs, and executive management.

The role will establish trusted enterprise data products and decision-ready analytics while respecting aviation record integrity, contractual obligations, export controls, data residency, and need-to-know access. A central priority is to improve the quality and usability of data from Ramco and connected systems so that leaders and front-line teams can manage aircraft availability, maintenance execution, material readiness, program performance, and financial results with greater confidence.

Top Aces Business Context

Top Aces provides advanced operational training and aircraft sustainment services to Canada, the United States, NATO members, and allied nations. The company operates globally in a safety-critical and security-sensitive environment that combines flight operations, maintenance and repair, engineering, supply chain, training, and proprietary technology. The data environment therefore requires strong governance across business units, legal entities, jurisdictions, and security domains.

The Director will translate these operating realities into an enterprise data strategy that supports growth, operational readiness, regulatory compliance, and disciplined investment. The role must balance standardization with the access boundaries required for Canadian, U.S., and international programs.

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Data Strategy and Operating Model

Partner with the CIO to develop and execute a multi-year enterprise data and BI strategy aligned with Top Aces' business strategy, operating model, technology roadmap, and investment priorities.
Create a practical data operating model that defines decision rights, ownership, stewardship, architecture standards, delivery methods, and support responsibilities across corporate and regional teams.
Chair or support the enterprise data governance council and maintain a prioritized roadmap based on operational value, regulatory risk, data quality, and delivery capacity.
Partner with the CIO and U.S. IT and security leadership to establish appropriate data segregation, access controls, and technology control plans for FOCI-related and export-controlled environments, where applicable.

Data Governance Quality and Protection

Establish enterprise policies and standards for data ownership, classification, quality, lineage, retention, archival, residency, access, and acceptable use.
Define authoritative sources and common business terms for critical domains, including aircraft, fleets, components, serialized parts, maintenance programs, work orders, defects, inventory, suppliers, customers, contracts, personnel, and financial dimensions.
Implement data quality controls, issue-management workflows, and scorecards that identify root causes and assign corrective action to accountable data owners.
Work with Cybersecurity, Legal, Export Compliance, Privacy, Quality, and program security personnel to protect personal, proprietary, controlled, and customer information throughout its lifecycle.
Ensure analytics and data-sharing practices comply with applicable contractual clauses, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR requirements, privacy laws, and customer security obligations.

Data Architecture Integration and Platforms

Define the target enterprise data architecture, including ingestion, integration, master and reference data, lakehouse or warehouse services, semantic models, reporting, metadata, and monitoring.
Establish integration patterns and data contracts for Ramco and other enterprise platforms using secure APIs, event-based interfaces, ETL or ELT pipelines, and controlled file exchange where required.
Reduce duplicate datasets and spreadsheet-dependent reporting by creating reusable, governed data products and certified semantic models.
Set engineering standards for observability, reconciliation, change control, testing, performance, resilience, backup, and recovery across the data platform.
Manage the data-platform lifecycle, capacity, licensing, vendor performance, and total cost of ownership, with particular attention to Microsoft Fabric, Azure data services, Power BI, and connected technologies.

Aviation and MRO Data

Lead data remediation and governance for Ramco MRO and ERP, focusing on master data, transactional integrity, usability, reporting structures, and interfaces with finance, supply chain, engineering, and flight operations.
Partner with Maintenance, Engineering, Airworthiness, Quality, Supply Chain, and Operations to improve the completeness and consistency of aircraft configuration, component history, flight hours and cycles, maintenance plans, work packages, defects, technical records, and inventory data.
Preserve the integrity and auditability of approved maintenance and airworthiness records while enabling controlled downstream analytics.
Develop trusted measures for aircraft availability, dispatch reliability, mission-capable status, maintenance schedule compliance, turnaround time, component reliability, inventory availability, and aircraft-on-ground events.
Support data readiness for operational and regulatory audits, customer reporting, contract performance reviews, and fleet-planning decisions.

Business Intelligence and Performance Management

Lead the design and delivery of executive, operational, and functional dashboards using consistent definitions, clear ownership, and traceable data sources.
Build an enterprise performance framework that connects mission delivery, safety, fleet readiness, maintenance, supply chain, program, customer, workforce, and financial measures.
Develop governed self-service analytics so business users can answer routine questions without creating uncontrolled copies of sensitive data.
Improve forecasting and scenario analysis for fleet utilization, maintenance demand, materials, labour capacity, contract delivery, revenue, cash flow, and program profitability.
Maintain a transparent intake and prioritization process for BI requests, balancing regulatory deadlines, operational urgency, enterprise reuse, and expected value.

Advanced Analytics and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and govern analytics and AI use cases such as predictive maintenance, component reliability, inventory optimization, demand forecasting, anomaly detection, and program risk monitoring.
Require documented business ownership, suitable data quality, human oversight, security review, and measurable benefits before analytics or AI solutions move into production.
Coordinate with engineering, operations, and technology teams when operational, training, mission-system, or live and synthetic data may be used, ensuring the work remains within approved classification and authorization boundaries.
Monitor model performance, data drift, access, and business outcomes, and retire solutions that no longer meet operational, security, or financial requirements.

Leadership and Stakeholder Partnership

Build and lead a capable team spanning data governance, architecture, engineering, BI, and analytics; define roles, develop talent, and manage succession for critical skills.
Partner with executives and functional leaders to convert business questions into governed data products, clear measures, and practical decisions.
Create an active network of business data owners and stewards and hold regular reviews of quality, adoption, access, and value realization.
Manage external partners and vendors through clear outcomes, architecture standards, service levels, security requirements, and commercial accountability.
Communicate data risks, progress, tradeoffs, and investment needs to senior leadership in concise business terms.

Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, data engineering, analytics, business, engineering, or a related discipline. A graduate degree or relevant professional certification is an asset.
At least 10 years of progressive experience in data management, analytics, BI, enterprise applications, or data architecture, including at least five years leading teams or major cross-functional programs.
Experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, MRO, or another highly regulated and asset-intensive industry is strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience improving data quality and reporting in a complex ERP or MRO environment. Direct experience with Ramco is a significant asset; experience with comparable aviation or enterprise platforms is also relevant.
Experience operating across multiple countries, legal entities, or security domains, including Canada and the United States, is preferred.

Technical and Regulatory Knowledge

Strong knowledge of enterprise data architecture, dimensional and semantic modelling, master data management, metadata, data quality, lineage, SQL, APIs, and ETL or ELT integration.
Hands-on understanding of modern cloud data platforms and BI technologies. Experience with Microsoft Fabric, Azure, Power BI, and Microsoft data services is preferred.
Working knowledge of aviation maintenance and supply-chain data, including serialized components, configuration, maintenance planning, technical records, reliability, and inventory transactions.
Familiarity with aviation regulatory and quality environments such as Transport Canada, FAA, EASA, safety management systems, and AS9100 is an asset.
Working knowledge of information classification, access control, auditability, privacy, data residency, the Canadian Controlled Goods Program, ITAR and EAR, CUI safeguards, CMMC, and NIST SP 800-171, as applicable to the role and programs supported.
Ability to obtain and maintain the security clearances, controlled-goods eligibility, and customer or program authorizations required for the position.

Leadership Competencies

Business judgment that connects data investment to safety, mission readiness, contract delivery, customer commitments, and financial performance.
Ability to influence executives, operational leaders, technical specialists, and front-line users without relying solely on formal authority.
Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to explain data limitations, security constraints, and architectural decisions to non-technical audiences.
Disciplined program leadership, with practical experience managing priorities, budgets, vendors, risks, and organizational change.
Commitment to Top Aces' values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together.

Provides coordination and project management within a strategic change context; oversees the development and implementation of plans; functions as a strategic resource to ensure that an optimal structure, design and implementation of the change(s) is/are in place to achieve desired outcomes and benefits; coordinates and aligns teams with other clinical initiatives to avoid duplication.
Provides clinical support to develop tools and templates for the team's review; utilizes best practice literature, guidelines and stakeholder expertise to draft tools and templates; identifies areas for integration and takes initiative to ensure tools and templates are efficient and effective.
Supports day-to-day management of the initiatives; completes work for the team, provides progress monitoring and reporting to steering committees including identification, management and mitigation/resolution of risks and issues; implements mitigation/resolution strategies.
Liaises with key support areas and stakeholders to ensure critical support outcomes are achieved; negotiates/facilitates resolution of any impediments to progress and success.
Applies change management principles to develop engagement strategies and action plans to maximize likelihood of success; builds relationships with stakeholders such as physicians to ensure input into clinical design, processes and outcomes.
Identifies and manages key stakeholder strategies and works closely with designated team and Communications to develop communication strategies.
Identifies and establishes appropriate team structure(s) and membership for initiatives including sponsorship, champion, clinical working, advisory or steering committee(s) and delivery and implementation teams.
Assesses and articulates the impact of initiatives from a systems perspective and manages the impacts and interdependencies with other initiatives at Fraser Health.
Assists in the development of project documentation (e.g. proposals, charters, work plans, risk management, plans, communication plans, etc.) as required.
Partners with the programs and other departments in the development, maintenance, and promotion of relevant goals and objectives; demonstrates relationship building for integrating with partners.
Participates in evaluation and refinement of tools and methods as required; assists in the development and presentation of project updates.

Qualifications

Education and Experience

Bachelor's Degree in Health Sciences or related field, Planning or Business Administration.

Seven (7) years' recent related clinical operations experience including planning, project management and/or organizational transformation or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

Competencies

Demonstrates the leadership practices of the Fraser Health Leadership Framework of Clear, Caring and Courageous and creates the conditions for people to succeed.

Professional/Technical Capabilities

Working knowledge of change and project management principles coupled with a strong understanding of the healthcare system and the clinical program that is being supported.
Knowledge of other health care disciplines and their role in health care.
Ability to motivate and influence leaders, physicians and staff at all levels to embrace and take action on transformation initiatives.
Diplomatic negotiation and interpersonal skills and ability to influence without formal authority.
Ability to provide leadership to a variety of project teams in an environment in which issues are constantly surfacing and priorities fluctuate routinely as new initiatives enter portfolio.
Ability to work independently and as a member of multi-disciplinary teams.
Ability to plan, organize and prioritize work.
Ability to operate a standard PC and effectively utilize a variety of software applications to support the initiative management activities.

Fraser Health is the heart of health care for over two million people in Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley in British Columbia, Canada, on the traditional, ancestral and unceded lands of the Coast Salish and Nlaka’pamux Nations and is home to 32 First Nations within the Fraser Salish region.

People - those we care for and those who care for them - are at the heart of everything we do. Our hospital and community-based services are delivered by a team of 50,000+ staff, medical staff and volunteers.

We are committed to planetary health and value diversity in the work force. We strive to maintain an environment of respect, caring and trust. Fraser Health’s hiring practices aspire to ensure all individuals are treated in an inclusive, equitable and culturally safe manner.

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible
